subject: Maths
title: Maths Exam 5
topic: Algebra 3: sequences, simultaneous equations · Non-calculator · Higher
intro: No calculator. For simultaneous equations, give both answers like x = 2, y = 3. Show your working in the box.

questions.q: Which of these is a geometric sequence?
Write down the next term of 7, 11, 15, 19, …
A sequence has nth term 4n − 9. Work out the 15th term.
A sequence has nth term 3n + 5. Is 100 a term in this sequence? Show how you decide.
questions.ms: No. M1 3n + 5 = 100 so 3n = 95, A1 n = 31.67 is not a whole number, so 100 is not a term.

questions.q: The geometric sequence 2, 6, 18, 54, … continues. Work out the 6th term.
A sequence starts at 3. The term-to-term rule is ‘multiply by −2’. Work out the 5th term.
questions.ms: 48. 3, −6, 12, −24, 48. M1 at least three terms with correct signs, A1.

questions.q: Pattern 1 uses 4 matchsticks, pattern 2 uses 7 and pattern 3 uses 10. How many matchsticks are in pattern 20?
questions.ms: 61. M1 goes up by 3, M1 nth term 3n + 1, A1 3 × 20 + 1 = 61.
x = 7, y = 3. M1 add to get 2x = 14, A1 x = 7, A1 y = 3.
x = 4, y = 2. M1 subtract to get 2x = 8, A1 x = 4, A1 y = 2.
x = 2, y = 3. M1 multiply second by 3 (15x − 3y = 21), M1 add: 17x = 34, A1 x = 2, A1 y = 3.

questions.q: 3 pens and 2 rulers cost £4.60. 1 pen and 2 rulers cost £2.60. Work out the cost of one pen and the cost of one ruler. Give your answers in pounds, like p = 1.20, r = 0.50.
questions.ms: Pen £1.00, ruler 80p. M1 3p + 2r = 4.60 and p + 2r = 2.60, M1 subtract 2p = 2.00, A1 p = 1, A1 r = 0.80.
4x⁶. B1 4, B1 x⁶ (square the 2 and double the power).

questions.q: Number revisit. Round each number to 1 significant figure to estimate 48.7 ÷ 0.24
questions.ms: 250. M1 50 ÷ 0.2, A1 250 (accept 200 from 50 ÷ 0.25 with M1 only). Bigger than 48.7 because we divide by less than 1.
